subject: Clarify metering & billing for hosted API: system messages, tool calls, rounding
messages:
From: Alex Brown <alex@fastanalytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-03T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Questions on hosted API metering: system tokens, tool calls, rounding

Hi Monica,

Quick one as we're finalizing our internal SOW: can you confirm how Redwood counts tokens for hosted API usage? We need a clear blurb for finance that covers these specific points so we can map to our own forecast tool: 

1) Are system messages (role: system prompts, guardrails injected by the runtime) billed as input tokens?
2) For function/tool calling flows: which parts count as input vs. output? For example, the model emits a function call (name + JSON args) and then our connector returns a 1.2kB JSON payload — how is that treated across requests?
3) Streaming and partial responses — do you bill tokens as they are streamed, and are there rounding quirks we should be aware of when we aggregate hourly usage?
4) Do you round at the per-request level or at aggregate (daily/monthly) billing? We have some integrations that send tiny requests at high QPS and small rounding could materially change our cost math.

Could you also attach the hosted-rate card and an example breakdown? We're trying to decide whether to include a 10% buffer in our forecast for rounding/overheads.

Thanks — Alex

Alex Brown
Head of Platform
FastAnalytics

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Brown <alex@fastanalytics.com>
Cc: Fiona Li <fiona@fastanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T10:35:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Questions on hosted API metering: system tokens, tool calls, rounding

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise summary you can paste into your SOW + an attached example CSV and the current hosted rate card (attached). Long-form details follow the summary.

SOW-friendly summary (short):
- Redwood bills both input and output tokens. System messages (the system role text injected at request time) count as input tokens.
- For function/tool flows: the tokens the model emits to request a function (name + JSON arguments) are billed as output tokens. Any external tool response that is then sent back into the model as a follow-up request is billed as input tokens on that subsequent request.
- Streaming: tokens are metered as they are generated; billing aggregates tokens at the request level. We report whole-token counts; each request's token total is rounded up to the nearest whole token before aggregation.
- Rounding and aggregation: rounding is applied per-request (i.e., we sum integers across requests for hourly/daily totals). In high-QPS, small-request scenarios the per-request rounding can introduce a measurable overhead — we typically recommend engineering teams batch short prompts when latency allows.

Attached: redwood-hosted-ratecard-202602.pdf, example-billing-breakdown.csv (small table showing sample prompt/output sizes and billed tokens).

Longer explanation + examples:
1) System messages: any system role content you pass in the chat request (or that our runtime injects) is tokenized and counted as input. Example: a 40-token system prompt + 120-token user prompt -> input = 160 tokens.

2) Function/tool calling (common gotchas):
- When the model emits a function call, the tokens representing the function name + JSON arguments are considered model output tokens (billed as output).
- If your connector invokes an external service with that JSON and then constructs a follow-up chat message to the model that includes the service response, the service response becomes input tokens on the next request and is billed as input.
- Example sequence: user prompt (300 tokens) -> model produces function call (output: 120 tokens) -> service returns 800-token JSON -> you send a follow-up request that includes the 800-token JSON as context (input: 800 + any system/user tokens). Billed tokens: request 1 billed for input 300, output 120; request 2 billed for input (800 + overhead).

3) Streaming and partial responses:
- We meter tokens as they are generated during streaming. For billing, we aggregate to the nearest whole token per request. If a single streaming response produces 342.6 internal token units, that is rounded up to 343 for that request.
- If you open multiple concurrent streams for the same logical conversation, each stream/request is rounded separately. This is why batching or fewer larger requests often reduces per-token overhead.

4) Aggregation and billing windows:
- Internally we sum integer token counts across requests for hourly/daily/monthly reporting. Rounding is per-request, not only at the invoice level.

5) Caching: Redwood's prefix/KV caching can reduce billed tokens when the cache provides a full or partial reply without needing the model to re-generate the cached content. Cache hits result in fewer model tokens and thus lower billed usage; however, cache behavior depends on your cache policy and TTLs. Cached tokens are not charged because the model was not executed to produce them.

If useful, I can provide a small spreadsheet modeling your current traffic with and without batching so you can see where rounding adds delta. I've attached a tiny example.

Cheers,
Monica

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-03T12:08:00-05:00
Subject: Fwd: Questions on hosted API metering — discount language?

Looping myself in — Monica, can you confirm how we should describe discounts/commits in the contract so finance doesn't get surprised by cache-driven variance? FastAnalytics typically asks for commit language that ties to "billed tokens" — do we need to specify exclusions for third-party tool traffic or cache-supplied tokens? Also, for large-commit discounts (e.g., >$75k/month), do we treat credits against billed tokens net of caching savings?

If you can propose 1-2 short contract clauses, I'll review with legal.

-Vivek

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Brown <alex@fastanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T13:24:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Questions on hosted API metering — discount language?

Counterparty-visible clause suggestion (short, SOW friendly):
"Billing is based on billed token usage as recorded by Redwood's metering system. Billed tokens include tokens generated by model inputs and outputs (including system messages and model-emitted function call tokens). Tokens returned by external connectors or caches that do not require model execution are not billed. Discounts and committed usage credits shall be applied against billed tokens as recorded in Redwood's invoices after accounting for caching and connector behavior."

Fallback, two-line alternative for simplicity:
"Billing is per billed token (input + output) as measured by Redwood. Committed usage credits apply to billed tokens after runtime-level caching and connector processing adjustments."

I recommend the first variant if the customer is technical (FastAnalytics is). It clarifies that credits are applied against actual billed tokens. If legal wants a cap, we can propose a reconciliation window (30 days) to handle disputes.

I also updated the attached example CSV to include a column showing "billed_tokens_after_rounding" so they can see rounding impact at their observed request sizes.

-Monica
